MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 8, 2020

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:03 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s Executive
Order N-29-20.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Members of Lion’s Heart – Griffin Gallien, Xander Lorraine, Nation Dixon – led the flag
salute.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Dev/Public Works Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF requested to remove item 5C from the Consent Calendar.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-B, and D-G AS
  FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF AUGUST 2020

  APPROVED WARRANTS 63138 THROUGH 63163 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $71,102.70 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 090120 THROUGH 090220;
  63149 (VOID); IN THE AMOUNT OF $77,836.26 FOR A GRAND TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $148,538.36 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

D.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF AUGUST 17, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 8, 2020
 E.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF AUGUST 19, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF AUGUST 25, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF AUGUST 31, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

REMOVED FOR INDIVIDUAL CONSIDERATION

C.  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA REGIONAL EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS
  COMMITTEE AND REGIONAL LAW ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE MINUTES OF
  MAY 14, 2020

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF commented that she is pleased that the Palos Verdes Peninsula
has a new Emergency Services Coordinator in place and suggested this person attend
future Emergency Preparedness trainings for Council Members, to make the training more
specific to the Peninsula.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  PRESENTATION FROM COX COMMUNICATIONS ON INFRASTRUCTURE
  UPGRADE

Michael Hadland and Kristen Camuglia from Cox Communications provided an update on
Cox’s recent upgrades and communication efforts within the community in light of COVID-
19. Changes in internet usage during the pandemic, network capacity upgrades including
the installation of new nodes, and 2020 customer communication efforts were outlined.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF stated that she recently received a door hanger notice for a
planned outage, which listed a 10-hour outage window. Ms. Camuglia explained the rolling
outage process with a two to four hour window throughout a service area, and that they are
working to reduce the length of the service windows. Ms. Camuglia explained that service
issues are handled on a case by case basis, and Cox tries to troubleshoot each case to
determine the best solution, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF. She also highlighted
the burden that security cameras require in terms of upload speeds.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN noted that the Dapplegray community experienced a
planned outage today, and inquired what specific work was being done. Mr. Hadland
explained that an additional node for enhanced service was being installed in that area.
COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated that the worst complaints he receives from the
community over the last two months involve issues with Cox Communications.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN discussed the services being received by Cox, and
performed a speed test in his home to compare it to the advertised speeds for the level of
service he pays for. Discussion ensued regarding speed tests on cell phones, over Wi-Fi
and on hard-wired devices.

Lastly, COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN noted the poor customer service received on a
recent call to Cox regarding a payment issue, and stated that he has received similar
complaints from residents in the community.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 8, 2020
 MAYOR SCHMITZ thanked Cox Communications for participating in this meeting, and for
continuing to engage with the City and community. She emphasized that the more
information City staff and Council Members have, the better informed the community will be.
She also reported that another follow-up meeting is scheduled between Cox, the Peninsula
Mayors and the School District.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  TREE MAINTENANCE SERVICES REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS – AWARD OF
  CONTRACT TO WEST COAST ARBORISTS

Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Superintendent Goldsmith explained the tree inventory system outlined by West Coast
Arborists (WCA) and the benefits, as well as the grid-pruning process, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER MITCHELL. She confirmed that smaller diameter tree removals will be handled by
staff to save on costs, and the larger trees will be removed by the contractor.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF discussed the hourly rate of WCA, versus that of Travers Tree
Service. She inquired about issues leading to the termination of the contract with Trimming
Land Care.

City Attorney Davis noted that although it is a five-year contract, the City can terminate the
contract with WCA at any time with or without cause.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated that he was very pleased with the selection of WCA,
noting that they are arborists and a very reputable company.

Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted that WCA maintained all of the tree inventory
up until the end of their contract in 2016, and will continue to use this when work begins under
the new contract.

Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted that the grid-trimming plan states that the City
has 5,000 trees with a schedule of 1,000 trees per year for 3-5 years, in response to MAYOR
PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN noted that the hourly rates listed for WCA is for one worker,
versus for three workers listed for Travers Tree Service.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN,
TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE ATTACHED FIVE-YEAR AGREEMENT WITH WEST COAST
  ARBORISTS FOR TREE MAINTENANCE SERVICES.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  CONSIDERATION OF PROGRAM TO PROMOTE USE OF ELECTRIC LAWN AND
  YARD MAINTENANCE EQUIPMENT AND GREEN ZONE CERTIFICATION FOR
  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 8, 2020
 American Green Zone Alliance (AGZA) representative Dan Mabe summarized the organization
and the certification process for the AGZA Green Zone Certification.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF confirmed that there would be no cost to the City for this program.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL made note for the record that she is a member of the Board
of South Coast Qir Quality Management District (AQMD) and although she has no financial
interest, AQMD funds the AGZA programs.

Discussion ensued regarding the transition process of equipment, the demonstration and
education process, potential of a gradual roll-out, and the minimum requirements for an AGZA
Green Zone Certification, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN.

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that this program is an educational opportunity for local
contractors and the community.

Mr. Mabe from AGZA explained that there is no penalty for going through the entire educational
process and not earning the certification. City Attorney Davis confirmed that this is an
introductory and educational program, with no obligations to the City within the contract.

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that the benefits and opportunities available must first
to be explained to the community, before addressing and establishing new policies within the
City, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN.

Mr. Mabe explained that the minimum requirement for certification is phasing out two-stroke
equipment for routine maintenance, in response MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN and COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL emphasized the
enormous emission reduction achieved by transitioning from gas to electric lawn equipment.

MAYOR SCHMITZ recapped the discussion, beginning with the resident who brought this topic
forward to the City Council earlier this year, and now realizing the greater need for education
and demonstration within the community, rather than an outright ban. She explained that the
Environmental Advisory Committee (EAC) requested the City Council consider education first,
before making any major policy decisions on this topic, which in turn will lead to greater
compliance and success in the long run.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO INITIATE OUTREACH/EDUCATIONAL EFFORTS
  RELATED TO TRANSITIONING LAWN AND MAINTENANCE EQUIPMENT
  FROM GAS-POWERED TO ELECTRIC, AND PROVIDE A PROGRESS
  REPORT TO THE EAC AND CITY COUNCIL IN SIX MONTHS; AND
  APPROVE THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH AGZA
  ESTABLISHING ERNIE HOWLETT PARK AS A CERTIFIED GREEN ZONE
  SITE.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer provided an update on the Los Angeles County Health Officer Order,
reporting that Los Angeles County is continuing to see a steady decrease in the number of new
cases. Barbershops and hair salons have been allowed to reopen at limited capacity, and more
restrictions are expected to be lifted if the decline continues.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 8, 2020
 Assistant City Manager Davis provided the following updates regarding upcoming City Events:
  • The Hills Are Alive Race is being held in a virtual-only format from September 12 –
  October 12, and registration is now open.
  • The City Celebration has been re-envisioned to include a birthday video featuring video
  clips from residents, businesses, Council and staff, as well as a 2020 time capsule.
  • The Mayor’s Breakfast Ride is also being re-envisioned. Early plans include a trail riding
  experience for residents, highlighting certain equestrian points of interest within the City.
  • The City held its first Ice Cream Social Distance Event on September 4 from 4:00pm –
  6:00pm at Ernie Howlett Park, which was a huge success with over 500 participants.
  Residents drove through while the Mayor and volunteers passed out pre-wrapped ice
  cream, goodie bags donated by Malaga Bank and craft kits donated by Home Depot.

MAYOR SCHMITZ expressed her gratitude to staff and the community for helping make the
Ice Cream Social event such a fun and successful community event.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired about the memo issued by the City Attorney regarding the
City’s political sign regulations. City Attorney Davis explained the enforceable size
requirements outlined in the City’s municipal code, noted that the regulations limiting the
posting of political signs to no sooner than 30 days prior to an election were not enforceable
under current law and will be amended in the future, and also explained the ability of
commercial property owners to substitute a noncommercial message, including a candidate
endorsement, for a commercial message on an existing sign. All candidates were provided this
updated information by the City Clerk at the time the City Attorney submitted his memo.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL reported on actions made at the California Air Resources
Board (CARB) meeting last week. The Board passed the Heavy-Duty Omnibus Regulation,
requiring a reduction in NOx emissions from heavy-duty trucks beginning in 2024. A
regulation requiring a reduction of emissions from all vessels that call at all ports of California
was also passed. The Board will be visiting three impacted communities this week in the
South Coast Air District Basin, regarding AB 617 to discuss emission reduction plans.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that there was a Neighborhood Watch Leadership
Council meeting on September 1, where fire prevention was discussed.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended a Zoom meeting of the California Medical Association’s
Grand Rounds, discussing the effectiveness of wearing face masks.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN reported that Southern California Association of
Governments (SCAG) Regional Council formally adopted Connect SoCal to meet the
mobility needs of the local communities.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN expressed concern about recent State legislation
regarding local control, and stated that regulations cannot be one size fits all for California
cities. He encouraged the Council to remain engaged to protect vulnerable communities.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN reported on a funding opportunity for the local cities
through the South Bay Cities Council of Government (SBCCOG) that can be used toward
portions of the General Plan Update to create more housing, such as ADUs.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN expressed concern regarding recent actions on housing
issues taken by the League of California Cities, and stated that nothing is more relevant to
local control than zoning.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN also reported there have been no West Nile Virus
infections in the last three months.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN also reported on the Clean Power Alliance Board meeting
last week.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
SEPTEMBER 8, 2020
 MAYOR SCHMITZ reported on her bi-monthly meetings with the Peninsula Mayors,
specifically the recent meeting with representatives from Cox Communications.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

MAYOR SCHMITZ commented on the recent announcement by the Promenade on the
Peninsula of the closing of the ice rink at the end of September.

MAYOR SCHMITZ also announced that a red flag warning is currently in effect, which was
sent out to residents via Alert South Bay (formerly Nixle). She also provided important fire
safety reminders and tips for the community.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation: one potential case

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

B.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATORS
  Government Code Section 54956.8
  Property: 25851 Hawthorne Blvd., Rolling Hills Estates, CA 90274
  City Negotiators: City Manager & Director of Community Development & PW
  Negotiating Party: Fitzpatrick Family
  Under Negotiation: Price and terms of payment

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL recused herself from item 13B.

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 9:47 P.M. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting to the next regular City
Council meeting on Tuesday, September 22, 2020 at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular
meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Velveth Schmitz
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
SEPTEMBER 8, 2020
